t: Yelü Dashi fled the Jin conquest of the Liao in 1124 with the 20,000 troops of the Kedun garrison, took Balasaghun in 1134 and made the Kingdom of Qocho, the Karluks and the Karakhanids his vassals.
At the Battle of Qatwan on 9 September 1141 the Khitans encircled and destroyed the Seljuk army of Ahmad Sanjar north of Samarkand, winning all of Transoxiana and Khwarazm's tribute.
The state called itself the Great Liao, kept the Chinese calendar, titles, coins and seals, and was ruled by two empresses in its own right, Xiao Tabuyan and Yelü Pusuwan.
dyk: In 1146 a Jin envoy refused to dismount before the regent Xiao Tabuyan and demanded she bow to the Son of Heaven; she had him executed, and the Jin learned his fate only in 1175 from deserters.
ev: Yelü Dashi flees north-west to the garrison of Kedun on the Orkhon River, wins the allegiance of its 20,000 troops and proclaims himself gurkhan.
Dashi conquers the Karakhanid city of Balasaghun; the Kankalis, Karluks, Kyrgyz and the Kingdom of Qocho become vassals, while a Khitan attack on the Jin ends in disaster.
On 9 September the Khitans destroy Ahmad Sanjar's Seljuk army at the Battle of Qatwan north of Samarkand; Transoxiana is lost to the Seljuks and Khwarazm becomes a vassal.
Yelü Dashi dies; his wife Xiao Tabuyan rules as regent with the titles of empress Gantian, Gurkhan and Dashi.
The Qara Khitai cross the Amu Darya to defeat Khwarazm for unpaid tribute and install Tekish as Khwarazm Shah on 11 December.
A Qara Khitai army invading Ghurid lands near Kurzuban is routed in a night attack with 12,000 losses; Balkh passes to the Ghurids.
The Naiman refugee Kuchlug, married to Yelü Zhilugu's daughter, revolts and captures the gurkhan while he is hunting; Zhilugu remains nominal ruler until his death two years later.
Pursued by Genghis Khan's general Jebe, Kuchlug is captured and decapitated; the Mongols complete the conquest of the former Qara Khitai lands by 1220.

f.capital: Balasagun (in modern Kyrgyzstan); first bases at Kedun on the Orkhon River (1124) and by the Emil river (1130)
f.founder: Yelü Dashi, who took the title gurkhan, 'universal khan'
f.predecessor: The Liao dynasty (907–1125) of the Khitans, conquered by the Jurchen Jin
f.successor: The Mongol Empire, after Kuchlug's usurpation of 1211 and his death in 1218; the Qutlugh-Khanid dynasty of Kirman for a Khitan remnant
